title: Protecting the Main Branch —

header.html: Explain why main is protected; set up required reviews and status checks; choose between branch protection rules and rulesets; use linear history, signed commits, merge queue and auto-merge; write a CODEOWNERS file; read a rejected push
Git 2.50.1 for the local parts; the GitHub documentation (read 2026-11-16) for the GitHub parts

toc.title: Why protect main, and what a rule can require
A local model: the push that gets rejected

html:
1Why protect main, and what a rule can require

Main is what the whole team builds and deploys from, so one careless push hurts everyone. Protection forces every change through a pull request, a review and green checks. The figure shows the gates between a branch and main.

A branch protection rule targets one branch, all branches or a name pattern. By default each rule blocks force pushes and deletion. Admins are exempt unless you turn on "Do not allow bypassing the above settings".

Setting What it requires
Require pull request reviews before merging The approvals you set
Require status checks before merging The named checks must succeed
Require conversation resolution before merging Every review thread resolved
Require signed commits Every commit carries a verified signature
Require linear history No merge commits; squash or rebase merging must be enabled
Require merge queue PRs merge through a queue
Lock branch Read-only, and it cannot be deleted
Restrict who can push to matching branches Only the people or apps you list

The review options add three switches: "Dismiss stale pull request approvals when new commits are pushed", "Require review from Code Owners" and "Require approval of the most recent reviewable push".

For status checks, "Require branches to be up to date before merging" is the strict mode and the default once checks are required. Three traps follow:

  1. The check name must match the job name.
  2. A workflow skipped by a filter leaves its required check Pending, so the PR waits forever.
  3. For the merge queue, the workflow must also listen to the merge_group event.

Two facts about signing: commits made in the web interface are signed by GitHub's own key, but commits created by Rebase and merge are not signed by GitHub.

Tip

. A required check is only as good as its trigger. Make sure the workflow runs on every PR, or the check can stay Pending.

2A local model: the push that gets rejected

Real protection runs on GitHub's servers, not in your clone. The demo builds only a model: a pre-receive hook in a bare repository that refuses every update of main. Make the hook executable with chmod +x. Install it after main exists.

Try it. Switch on the model, then push to main.

#!/bin/sh
# origin.git/hooks/pre-receive: a local model of a protected main
while read old new ref; do
  if [ "$ref" = "refs/heads/main" ]; then
    echo "Protected branch: main accepts changes only through a pull request." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done
exit 0

git push

remote: Protected branch: main accepts changes only through a pull request.
 ! [remote rejected] main -> main (pre-receive hook declined)

The remote: line comes from the server. A force push and git push origin --delete main are rejected the same way. GitHub words its message differently, but the idea is the same. The way forward is a branch.

Try it. Move the commit to a branch and push that.

git switch -c add-footer
git branch -f main origin/main
git push -u origin add-footer

 * [new branch]      add-footer -> add-footer

Next the demo moves main inside the bare repository, to model what GitHub's merge button does once the rules are met. A second hook models Require linear history.

Try it. Push main with a merge commit into a repository that demands linear history.

git merge --no-ff add-cart
git push origin main

remote: Linear history required: merge commits are not allowed on main.
 ! [remote rejected] main -> main (pre-receive hook declined)

After git reset --hard origin/main, a rebase and git merge --ff-only, the push is accepted.

Tip

. When a push to main is rejected, do not fight the rule. Put the commits on a branch, push it and open a pull request.

3Rules or rulesets

Rulesets are an alternative to branch protection rules. The documentation calls them more flexible and says they have advantages, but it does not call them the recommended choice.

Topic Branch protection rule Ruleset
How many apply Only one rule per branch Several at once; rules aggregate and the most restrictive version wins
Targets A branch, all branches or a pattern Branches or tags, by pattern
Exemptions Admins are exempt unless the setting for admins is on Roles, teams or GitHub Apps can be exempted

A ruleset can be Active or Disabled without deleting it, and anyone with read access can view active rulesets. The limits are 75 per repository and 75 organization-wide, tied to the Team and Enterprise plans. Rulesets also layer with branch protection rules. Push rulesets (private and internal repositories) block pushes by file path, path length, file extension or file size.

4Merge queue, auto-merge and CODEOWNERS

A merge queue merges PRs into a busy protected branch after the required checks succeed. It tests each PR against the latest target branch plus the PRs ahead of it, and the buttons read "Merge when ready" and "Confirm merge when ready". CI can be GitHub Actions or another provider. Check the plan requirements for your account.

Auto-merge is switched on with "Allow auto-merge" in Settings, General, Pull Requests. It appears only on PRs that cannot merge yet, and it is disabled if someone without write access pushes to the PR.

A CODEOWNERS file names who must review which paths. It lives in .github/, the root or docs/ (the first one found, in that order), and it must be on the PR's base branch. Patterns work like .gitignore, and the last matching line wins.

Owners are @username, @org/team-name or an email, need write access, and sit on one line. Invalid lines are skipped, paths are case-sensitive, and the file stays under 3 MB.

Try it. This file has five lines. The demo asks Git's own ignore matcher which lines match and keeps the last.

cat .github/CODEOWNERS

# .github/CODEOWNERS
*                    @shop/maintainers
*.js                 @shop/frontend
/docs/               @shop/docs
/payments/           @shop/payments @ada
/.github/CODEOWNERS  @shop/admins
Path Owner Why
src/app.js @shop/frontend *.js is later than *
docs/app.js @shop/docs Both match; the later line wins
payments/charge.py @shop/payments, @ada Two owners on one line
src/docs/x.md @shop/maintainers The leading slash anchors /docs/ to the root

To make owners mandatory, enable "Require review from Code Owners" in a rule or a ruleset. Approval from any one listed owner is enough. For a PR from a fork, GitHub reads the base branch's file. Protect the file itself with an entry for /.github/CODEOWNERS.

Tip

. Order CODEOWNERS from general to specific. Because the last match wins, a broad line placed at the end overrides every line above it.

5Practice Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Ada pushes her local main straight to the protected main and sees "remote rejected". What should she do?

  • APush again with --force so that the rule is ignored
  • BMove her commit to a branch, push it and open a pull request
  • CDelete the remote main and push her copy as the new main
  • DAsk a teammate to approve the push from the command line
Show the answer

Answer: B. Protection sends all changes through a branch and a pull request, and a force push is blocked too.

S2A required check named build stays Pending on a docs-only PR, because the workflow has a filter that skips docs changes. Why can the PR not merge?

  • AA workflow skipped by a filter leaves its required check Pending
  • BRequired checks never run on PRs that change only docs files
  • CThe check must first be approved by a reviewer on the PR
  • DPending checks count as a success after an hour goes by
Show the answer

Answer: A. The check never reports, so the merge box keeps waiting for it.

S3An admin merged a PR without the required approval, because admins are exempt by default. Which setting closes that gap?

  • ARestrict who can push to matching branches
  • BDismiss stale pull request approvals on new commits
  • CDo not allow bypassing the above settings
  • DRequire conversation resolution before merging
Show the answer

Answer: C. That setting applies the rules to admins as well.

S4A CODEOWNERS file lists *.js @shop/frontend and later /docs/ @shop/docs. Bob changes docs/app.js. Who owns the change?

  • A@shop/frontend, because the first matching line wins
  • BBoth teams, because every matching line adds owners
  • CNeither team, because a folder line cannot match a file
  • D@shop/docs, because the last matching line wins
Show the answer

Answer: D. Both lines match, and the last matching pattern wins.

S5An organization and a repository each want their own rules on main, and both must apply at the same time. Which feature allows that?

  • ATwo branch protection rules on the same branch of the repository
  • BA CODEOWNERS file with one entry for each of the two groups
  • CRulesets, which layer and apply the most restrictive version
  • DA locked branch, which holds the rules of both owners
Show the answer

Answer: C. Only one branch protection rule applies at a time, while several rulesets can apply together.

S6"Require linear history" is on. Which merge methods can the team still use?

  • AMerge commit and squash, because both add a single commit
  • BSquash and rebase, because neither adds a merge commit
  • COnly the merge commit, because it keeps the whole story
  • DAll three, because the setting only affects direct pushes
Show the answer

Answer: B. Linear history needs squash or rebase merging, which add no merge commit.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What does a branch protection rule block by default?

Show the answer

Force pushes and deletion of the branch.

R2Where can the CODEOWNERS file live?

Show the answer

In .github/, the root or docs/.

R3Which workflow event must be listened to for the merge queue?

Show the answer

merge_group.

R4Which check setting is the strict mode?

Show the answer

"Require branches to be up to date before merging".

R5How many branch protection rules apply to one branch at a time?

Show the answer

One.

R6Why is the pre-receive hook in the demo only a model?

Show the answer

Real protection runs on GitHub's servers.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Why every change goes through a PR, review and checks
Defaults a rule blocks force pushes and deletion; admins are exempt unless the admin setting is on
Reviews dismiss stale approvals; require Code Owners; approve the most recent push
Status checks name matches the job; skipped workflow means Pending; strict means up to date
History and signing linear history needs squash or rebase; web commits signed by GitHub, rebase merges not
Rules vs rulesets one rule per branch; rulesets layer, most restrictive wins, limits of 75, exempt list
Merge queue tests PRs in order; workflows need merge_group
Auto-merge "Allow auto-merge" in Settings, General; off after a push without write access
CODEOWNERS .github/, root or docs/; gitignore-style; last match wins
Local model pre-receive hook shows a rejected push; real rules run on GitHub
